record.original_question: For fixed r >= 1 and m edges, which B_{2,r+1}-free non-bipartite graph has the largest spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. What is the extremal graph attaining the maximum spectral radius over all B2,r+1-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer r ≥ 1, let B_{2,r+1} denote the book graph consisting of r+1 triangles sharing a common edge (equivalently, the graph obtained by joining a single edge to r+1 isolated vertices, so that K_2 ∨ \overline{K_{r+1}}). A graph G is called B_{2,r+1}-free if it does not contain B_{2,r+1} as a subgraph. The spectral radius ρ(G) of a graph G is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Fix r ≥ 1 and let m be a positive integer. Among all non-bipartite, B_{2,r+1}-free graphs with exactly m edges, determine the maximum possible value of ρ(G) and characterize all extremal graphs attaining this maximum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open question concerning spectral extremal graphs avoiding the book B_{2,r+1} among non-bipartite graphs of fixed size m. Related results address K_{2,r+1}-free graphs, non-bipartite graphs forbidding short odd cycles, and θ-free non-bipartite graphs of given size, but a complete solution for the non-bipartite B_{2,r+1}-free case with m edges does not appear in the located literature.

status_evidence.title: The Maximum Spectral Radius of Non-Bipartite Graphs Forbidding Short Odd Cycles
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral extremal results for non-bipartite graphs forbidding short odd cycles, with edges m fixed.
status_evidence.claim: Related spectral extremal problems for non-bipartite graphs of given size are actively studied but do not address B_{2,r+1}-free directly.

status_evidence.title: Non-bipartite graphs without theta subgraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the maximum spectral radius of non-bipartite graphs without theta subgraphs.
status_evidence.claim: Companion work on related forbidden subgraphs in non-bipartite graphs is recent and ongoing, suggesting the B_{2,r+1} case remains open.
